summary: Chicken gizzards simmered tender and tossed in a peppery tomato and bell pepper sauce with cubes of golden fried plantain.
story: Gizdodo joins gizzard with dodo, fried plantain, in a spicy sauce. It is a popular party dish and small chop at Nigerian celebrations.

items.name: Vegetable oil
items.note: for frying plantain, plus 3 tbsp for the sauce

steps.title: Cook the gizzards
steps.text: Place the gizzards in a pot with the sliced onion, cubes, thyme and salt. Add water to cover and simmer for 40 to 50 minutes, or 20 minutes in a pressure cooker, until tender when pierced. Keep 1/2 cup of the stock.

steps.title: Fry the plantain
steps.text: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the plantain cubes in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and slightly crisp on the edges. Drain on paper towels.

steps.title: Blend the base
steps.text: Blend the red peppers, tomato, scotch bonnet and half the onion until almost smooth. Boil in a dry pot for 8 to 10 minutes to evaporate excess water.

steps.title: Fry the sauce
steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a pan, fry the sliced onion and garlic for 2 minutes, then add the reduced blend and curry. Fry 10 to 12 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and the oil separates.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the gizzards and a splash of stock. Stir to coat and cook another 5 minutes until the gizzards are glazed. Season with salt.

steps.title: Add the plantain
steps.text: Fold in the fried plantain gently just before serving so it keeps its crisp edges. Garnish with diced green pepper and serve warm.

tips: Gizzards must be tender. Cook them until a fork enters easily before saucing.
Add the plantain at the last moment or it will go soggy.
Use ripe but firm plantains for neat cubes.
Pat the gizzards dry if you want an extra fried finish.

swaps.swap: Use diced chicken thigh or chicken hearts. Chicken thigh needs only 20 minutes of cooking.
Habanero or a milder red chilli.
